All 9 tests pass now (4 were failing before). I made one small change in each source file and didn't touch the tests.

**Bug 1: off-by-one in `splitBill`** (`src/bill.js`)
The leftover check used `i <= leftover`, so one extra person always got an extra cent. With an even split, where the leftover is 0, the first person still got 1 cent too many: `[301, 300, 300]` for 900 split 3 ways. This broke three tests, including the one checking that the total is preserved. I changed it to `i < leftover`, so exactly `leftover` people get the extra cent.

**Bug 2: `parseDuration` accepted trailing junk** (`src/duration.js`)
The parser picked out every number-plus-unit piece anywhere in the string and only threw an error if it found none. So `"10m and change"` was quietly read as 600 seconds. I added an anchored check, `/^(\d+[hms])+$/`, so the whole string has to be number-plus-unit pieces with nothing else. The unchanged regex still calculates the total. The check also rejects input that has junk before or between the pieces, like `"x10m"` or `"1h 30m"`.
